claim_text: Iron requirements increase during pregnancy to support maternal and fetal needs; whether a pregnant person needs a separate iron supplement and at what dose depends on antenatal guidance, laboratory findings and iron already present in prenatal products.
health_goal_or_outcome: Support safe assessment of iron intake during pregnancy without duplicate or inappropriate dosing.

population.age_range: Pregnant adolescents and adults; age-specific requirements differ.
population.other_context: Country-specific screening and supplementation policies vary.

ingredient_form_or_preparation: Dietary iron and supplemental elemental iron; prenatal multivitamins may already contain iron.
evidence_summary: NIH ODS Iron Health Professional Fact Sheet provides pregnancy-specific reference intake and safety information; antenatal policies should be checked locally.
limitations: Reference intake is not automatically a prescribed supplemental dose.
Ferritin, hemoglobin, tolerability and existing products influence clinical decisions.
